We've now explored the full picture — the core flows, the large-collection tooling, and the empty, oversized, error, and timing corners. Here's everything that's settled, in plain terms:

**Saving & revisiting**
- Save any page from a single address box; it's auto-enriched with a real title and short description, and the newest sits on top.
- Click a saved item to open the original in a new tab.

**Describing & organizing**
- Tag links (reuse your existing tags for consistency, or create new ones), shown right on each card.
- Add notes in simple Markdown, with a tidy two-line preview that expands.
- Rename or fully edit a link — title, address, and description.

**Finding**
- Live search across everything at once, plus precise queries: `#tag`, "exact phrases", AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, case-insensitive.

**Keeping a calm library**
- Reading list (opt-in) and Archive (hides links recoverably), as separate views.
- A preserved copy of every link so it survives even if the original changes or vanishes — readable content for pages, the original file for PDFs; a fixed snapshot you refresh only when you choose.

**Staying trustworthy & uncluttered**
- Duplicate-prevention when you save something already in your library.
- Permanent delete with a clear confirmation (no accidental loss).
- Sorting (newest / oldest / title) and safe multi-select bulk actions — tag/untag, read/unread, archive, delete — always scoped to exactly what you've selected.
- Friendly empty states, tidy handling of huge content, graceful errors for unreachable pages and non-addresses, and nothing that expires on its own.

That's **12 settled flows** covering everything from your original goal plus the management essentials you added.

I've noted a few polish items for later (how dates display, automatic retries, and the practical limits/storage of preserved copies) — none of which block building.

**May I now switch from exploring to actually building this as a real web application?** Once you approve, I'll move into development and construct it for real (not the exploratory prototype), then verify it against everything we've agreed.
